method_note: The OpenFEC JSON API and OpenSecrets could not be read with the fetch tool available (empty responses), so no per-donor FEC name search was possible. Large contributions were confirmed against the receiving committees' own itemised Schedule A filings on docquery.fec.gov (primary). Other items rely on reporting of FEC filings and are labelled that way. A total of 0 with status needs-check means 'nothing found', not 'confirmed zero'. Totals exclude spouses, ex-spouses, children and companies/corporate PACs.

people.name: Larry Page
people.note: Nothing found. The FEC-derived billionaire-family sheet from Americans for Tax Fairness (an advocacy group) shows $0 in contributions of $5,000 or more for 1 Jan 2023 to 28 Oct 2024. SCMP (Oct 2024) says he made no large donations. Gifts under $5,000 and Nov-Dec 2024 were not checked. His foundation pays almost all its grants to donor-advised funds, so any political routing would be invisible.

people.name: Jeff Bezos
people.note: Nothing found for Jeff himself. The ATF sheet's 'Bezos' family row (~$7.1m) is mostly his parents Jacklyn and Miguel Bezos giving to the bipartisan veterans super PAC With Honor Fund II. Excluded. His own $10m to With Honor was in 2018, outside the cycle. Amazon's $1m to the Trump inaugural fund (Dec 2024) is corporate and not an election contribution. An unsupported search-summary claim of '$7 million to Biden-Harris' was rejected. Small gifts were not checked.

people.name: Michael Dell
people.note: Nothing found. ATF sheet shows $0 in gifts of $5,000 or more (Jan 2023 to Oct 2024). He may have made small gifts (up to $5,000 a year) to the Dell Technologies PAC (C00369751); this is unverified because docquery rate-limited. Dell PAC's own candidate gifts are corporate PAC money, not his. The $6.25bn 'Trump Accounts' pledge (Dec 2025) is charitable and out of cycle.

people.name: Sergey Brin

outside.what: Catalyst4 (Brin-funded 501(c)(4)) grant in 2023 to Sixteen Thirty Fund (left-leaning 501(c)(4)). The filing labels it an environmental grant, so it is not clearly election money. Sourced only to InfluenceWatch/Inside Philanthropy; do not chart

people.note: No 2023-24 federal contribution by Brin himself was found. ATF's 'Brin' family row (~$16.7m) is ex-wife Nicole Shanahan's RFK Jr. giving; the divorce was final Sept 2023, so it is excluded. His reported Republican turn falls outside this cycle: RNC gifts in 2025 and California ballot money in 2026. Small gifts not checked.

people.name: Mark Zuckerberg

recipients.name: Meta Platforms, Inc. PAC (C00502906, bipartisan corporate PAC)
recipients.source: FEC filing FEC-1863144 (year-end 2024), Schedule A: Mark E. Zuckerberg, Menlo Park CA, 12/20/2024, $5,000

people.note: Fortune (Sept 2024, from FEC data) says he gives only through Meta's PAC, not directly to candidates. people.name: Larry Ellison

outside.what: About $45m to an undisclosed political nonprofit backing Trump's 2024 effort, per WSJ citing people familiar; not in FEC data

people.note: The widely cited ~$30-35m to Opportunity Matters Fund was given in 2021-22 (2022 cycle) and is excluded. In 2023 OMF Inc. moved $10m to OMF Action, which sent $10.8m to Trust in the Mission PAC (Scott's presidential super PAC). That is largely his 2022 money being transferred, not new giving. CNBC (Apr 2024): no federal donation by him so far in 2024. WSJ (2026): FEC shows nothing from him to Trump campaign/PACs. Son David Ellison's $929,600 to Biden Victory Fund excluded. OMF Inc.'s year-end 2023 and 2024 termination reports and small candidate gifts were not checked. Claims of '$50m+ to Preserve America PAC' come from unreliable sites and are disregarded.

people.name: Jensen Huang
people.note: No reporting or FEC trace found of any 2023-24 federal contribution by Jensen or Lori Huang. Proving zero requires an FEC name search, which was not possible. His 2025 Trump ties (Nvidia-related) are out of cycle and corporate.

people.name: Steve Ballmer

outside.what: $100m+ to USAFacts (nonpartisan nonprofit) incl. 2024 'Just the Facts' campaign; Forbes calls it a twist on political giving but it is not campaign money

people.note: Total left null (unknown, NOT zero). Forbes (Oct 2024, citing FEC) gives only a 2017-2024 window: ~$38,000 to five Democratic candidates and $40,000+ to the DCCC. His 2024-cycle amount is therefore somewhere between $0 and ~$78k, all Democratic. Wife Connie Ballmer gave ~$1.25m to pro-Harris groups this cycle (Forbes); excluded.

people.name: Warren Buffett
people.note: Fortune (Sept 2024, citing FEC data): his last federal donation was Nov 2019 ($106,500 to the DCCC and $2,800 to Mark Kelly). Bloomberg says he has avoided donating to federal candidates. Berkshire stated in Oct 2024 that he does not endorse or support candidates. Not checked against FEC ourselves, and Oct-Dec 2024 not ruled out by FEC review. Beware false matches with 'Warren for Senate' (Elizabeth Warren).
